text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: canary deployment v13 encoder — p99 latency breach detected in eu-west-1. Auto-page sent to #incidents and on-call. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/encoder-canary-v13

alex: seeing p95 ~120ms -> 550ms and p99 spiking to ~1.2s on streaming endpoints. Canary traffic at 20%.

mira: confirmed on traces — large tail on "hotpath" requests with long KV lock waits. Looks like KV cache misses + model variant fallback loop.

jonah: observability: "encode_stream_latency" spike at 18:02 UTC, coincides with canary traffic ramp. Sampled logs show repeated `Retrying segment upload` for long requests.

priya: paging SRE now. @samir are you able to join for immediate rollback if needed?

samir: joining. pulling canary job details. running `redwoodctl rollout status canary/v13`

alex: stack traces attached in logs — small fraction of requests hit a new path in the encoder that does additional lookup + quant decode. Maybe a regression in async IO.

incident-bot: Paging: @sre-oncall (samir) @platform-oncall (jonah) — escalation window started. Severity: S2.

samir: mitigation options from quick checklist:
- throttle canary to 5%
- pause canary ramp
- force traffic to v12 (stable) for streaming routes
- enable per-route fallback to v12 encoder
Which do we want asap?

mira: prefer quick throttle + enable fallback. Rolling rollback might be slower due to running connections. Throttle to 5% and enable fallback for streaming.

priya: agree. I'll patch routing policy now. Doing: `redwood route set canary-weight --service=encode-stream --weight=5%`

jonah: while priya does that, I'm flipping on fallback: `redwood config set /services/encode-stream/fallback_model v12 --scope live` (will propagate to edge).

alex: routed to v12 for new requests confirmed in logs around 18:07 UTC. p95 back down to ~150ms, p99 trending down but still ~650ms (draining long-lived streams).

samir: starting controlled rollback plan if tail doesn't recover: 1) scale up v12 pods x2 for capacity 2) disable v13 entirely 3) notify customers. Do we have capacity margin?

mira: infra has ~30% spare in eu-west-1, scaling OK. But long-lived streaming sessions need forceful reconnects to fully recover tail.

priya: alerted product and account team for impacted customers. Notifying top clients: AcmeChat and Sparkline. Draft message ready: "We detected elevated latency for streaming during canary roll. We throttled canary and applied fallback; we are monitoring and will follow up."

jonah: seeing stream stall metric `stream_chunk_delay` — a subset of sessions are stuck in resend loop. Recommend increasing `stream_chunk_timeout` to 8s temporarily to avoid quick retries piling up.

alex: increasing to 8s now. Command: `redwood config patch --path /services/encode-stream/stream_chunk_timeout --value 8s`

incident-bot: CHANGE: canary weight set to 5% by priya at 18:06:21 UTC. Fallback applied to v12 at 18:06:45 UTC.

samir: p99 now ~320ms at 18:12 UTC and continuing down. Good signal. Scaling v12 + chunk timeout seems to help.

mira: important: capture traces for the 200 worst requests in the canary window for RCA. Jonah can you export?

jonah: exporting and uploading to drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/encoders/canary-v13-traces/3555001234.zip

priya: customer update sent. CS reports one session reconnect required for AcmeChat — they were notified and saw no data loss.

alex: plan for next 60m: keep canary at 5%, monitor p99/p50 streaming, let long-lived sessions drain, collect artifacts. If we remain stable, schedule a rollback to v12 tomorrow with full verification.

samir: I'm going to start the incident timeline and notify on-call rotation for handoff at 20:00 UTC. Add follow-ups:
- RCA owner: mira
- Telemetry: jonah (collect traces + metrics)
- Deploy/tests: alex (repro case + test harness)
- Customer comms: priya

mira: quick notes for RCA: possible root causes to validate — async IO regression in v13 encoder, additional quant decode path, cache key change causing miss storm, and increased retry logic surface.

priya: also confirm whether throttling at 5% had any measurable customer impact on request success rates (was error rate increased due to fallback?).

jonah: I'll run a canary vs baseline perf diff and include in notes.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by samir. Handoff scheduled to on-call @ 20:00 UTC. Severity remains S2; mitigations applied.

alex: closing thread for live paging — we'll keep this thread for follow-up and RCA artifacts. If anything regresses, re-open paging. :white_check_mark:
